versions.changelog:
Consent defined as a live condition rather than a stored yes: it exists in the overlap of everyone's active constraints, and dissolves when that overlap does
Two working resolutions, Task and Field, so small bounded work never carries the weight of a long relationship, and escalation between them is announced rather than silent
Friction shifts to holding: hesitation, latency, and silence halt progression and offer one low-stakes anchor, never a demand for clarification and never a prompt for data
Earth and Kinship named as veto-bearing, with metabolic ceilings for energy, water, and heat, and unmeasurable costs declared unknown rather than quietly omitted
Exit built as a soft landing: portable data return, no shadow profile of an absence, and care continuity that holds the connection until a person, a community, or another system can take it up
Lineage credited to disability justice, transformative justice, and Indigenous data governance, read as ours rather than spoken for them
A one-minute version and a machine-carriable form, so the whole thing is usable at any size an agent or a person can hold

A governance skill that treats consent as a live relational condition across humans, agents, and ecological systems with the hope of enabling interaction without coercion, extraction, or irreversible harm-accumulation.
